avoid: A public sharing switch that creates an outside link is too open for clinical scenarios, which are the center's own work.
clickup 9e0d5df7.fit: Scenario manager: add 'save as template' with access set per template (private, chosen people, or the whole organization). That is simpler than today's unclear SCE permissions.

steal: Each checklist row has its own assignee, so tasks can be split between roles such as the sim tech and faculty.
The section header shows progress ('Checklists 0/N') and a filter for the items assigned to you ('N for me').
'Use Template' sits beside 'Add checklist', so a set of items can be reused on other tasks.
'+ New checklist item' adds a row without leaving the task.
avoid: There is no scoring, no required flag and no rubric weighting, which is too thin for learner evaluation checklists.
clickup 456a85db.fit: Scenario manager: extend the cut-down Case Manager checklist with assignees and reusable templates. Essentials evaluations would still need scoring and a set time for filling them in, and this does not cover QR without login.

steal: The When/Then blocks are summed up in one plain sentence under the work area.
A warning appears right away when an action will be skipped because the assignee lacks access.
The assignee picker includes roles that fill themselves in, such as 'Task creator', 'Triggered by' and 'Watchers'.
After a rule is created, the Manage tab shows how many rules are active or inactive, with an on/off switch for each.
avoid: Full libraries of integrations and rule catalogs across many categories are heavier than the few defaults a scenario needs (auto-record, prep email, announcements).
clickup e17ac016.fit: Scenario manager: turn today's auto-record, email and announcement settings on scheduling templates into a clear When/Then panel of defaults per scenario. Keep the presets few; this is not a general automation product.

steal: Three cards set access: Team (can use, not edit), Community, and Only me.
The Team option says plainly that team members can use the template but not edit it.
Choosing Community shows an 'In review' label on the list after saving, because the community is moderated.
A 'Highlight your contribution' switch decides whether your name is shown publicly.
avoid: Publishing to a public community of all product users is wrong for Essentials, which needs sharing by organization and role, not a global template marketplace.
heidi 4b33f07a.fit: Scenario manager: the best nearby model for simpler sharing per scenario (private, team can use only, or a moderated organization library) instead of today's unclear SCE access.

steal: 'Duplicate' is in each row's menu, so you can copy a template without opening the editor.
The new row is renamed automatically with '(Copy)' at the end.
A short message confirms 'Template duplicated'.
The Visibility column ('Just me', 'Community In review') stays in view while you duplicate.
heidi 5e3fe2a1.fit: Scenario manager: add a one-click duplicate from the library, so faculty can start from an existing scenario instead of a blank form or a Word import.

steal: A multiple-choice list asks 'Which event type will this apply to?', next to 'Apply to all, including future event types' (screens 3-7).
The rule reads top to bottom: when it runs (before the start, plus an offset), then 'Do this' action cards (screens 3-8).
Placeholders such as {EVENT_NAME} and {ATTENDEE} fill in the email subject and text (screens 8, 10).
The list card shows what triggers the workflow and says 'Active on N event type' (screen 12).
avoid: Across 12 screens it only offers reminders by email or text message, with none of the auto-record or announcement actions Essentials needs per phase.
cal-com f693c13b.fit: Scenario manager: the best match for automation per scenario. A reusable When/Do rule set is attached to chosen event types, like SCE templates, and covers today's prep-email and auto-record defaults.

steal: The Products area has 'Search', 'Browse' and 'Add custom item' in one row, so catalog items and free text sit together.
The product picker shows how many of each variant are available, keeps 'Add' disabled until something is chosen, and counts selections out of 500.
An unsaved draft offers 'Discard' or 'Save'; once saved, 'Duplicate' and 'Share' sit at the top of the draft.
A Notes box sits to the right of the items, so setup notes stay next to the equipment list.
avoid: Payment, invoice and 'Mark as paid' controls belong to selling and clash with a sim equipment list.
shopify 5421.fit: Scenario manager: the best model to replace the free-text Equipment & Supplies field with items linked to inventory, quantities and notes. Check-out stays in Inventory, and the draft stage extends SCE editing.

arcade 9b7b370a.summary: From the library, the user picks how to create a demo, fills in a step, sets preview options, then reviews engagement and where viewers drop off at each step.
steal: The start screen groups the recording options ('Chrome Extension', 'Desktop App') under a Popular label, next to uploading or turning a video into a demo (screen 2).
An empty step offers two sets of sources: add from your computer, the library or another demo, or capture with the extension, desktop app or Figma (screen 3).
Edit, Preview and Insights tabs keep editing, the learner's view and completion data in one project (screens 4-8).
A chart shows how many viewers carry on or drop off at each step ('From Step N: conversion / drop-off %') (screen 8).
avoid: Sample data and an Upgrade banner at the end of editing are a warning: completion data for the pre-brief should not sit behind a paywall (screens 6-8).
arcade 9b7b370a.fit: Scenario manager: grow today's Briefing tab video into the planned interactive orientation and pre-brief maker, with an outline and clickable spots. The preview switches map to what learners see before a session. Do not copy Arcade's sales-demo insights and buttons wholesale.

arcade 644ef98c.summary: On a demo step, the user edits the text of a clickable callout, generates a voiceover from that text, then reviews the voiceover timeline with 'Edit voiceover'.

steps.1: Clickable spot settings: text and 'Generate voiceover'
steps.2: Voiceover timeline under the work area

steal: The written callout text is the only source for 'Generate voiceover', so one script drives both the caption and the audio (screen 1).
Clickable spots come in three styles (Hotspot, Area, Callout) and can be set to 'Open by default' (screen 1).
Each clickable spot can jump to another step, chosen from a list (screen 1).
After generating, a voiceover timeline at the bottom shows the sound wave, the length and 'Edit voiceover' (screen 2).
arcade 644ef98c.fit: Scenario manager: supports the new interactive orientation maker with narration per step. It is also a pattern for scripts (a written cue, then optional audio) without a Maestro-style stage editor.

steal: Before any templates exist, the screen explains why they help and offers 'Create' twice, at the top and in the middle (screen 1).
The new-template pop-up asks for a name first, then offers 'Build branded' or 'Customize from gallery' (screens 2-3).
Previews of each slide type (chart, sample, text) update live while you set brand colours and upload a font (screens 4-7).
A 'You are editing a template' banner stays visible, 'Publish this template?' offers Keep draft or Publish, and library cards then show a Draft label (screens 8-10).
avoid: A full presentation style builder (fonts, chart styles, slide layouts) is too much for the deliberately basic SCE editor, which should not become a Maestro-style tool.
pitch 593.fit: Scenario manager: a strong pattern for scenarios in an organization library: start blank or from the gallery, keep drafts apart from published versions, and share on publish. It extends today's SCE editor without turning it into a slide product.

steal: Notes for each slide sit in a side panel while the slide stays visible (screens 2-3).
The empty panel shows 'Add speaker notes…' until something is written (screen 2).
After the panel closes, a dot on the notes icon shows that notes exist (screen 4).
pitch f0c62f24.fit: Scenario manager: a light pattern for SP or faculty scripts and cues in each scenario phase. It extends Briefing without a branching Maestro editor, and notes that only the presenter sees map to cue cards per role.

tally 908fac0b.summary: From an empty forms page, the author creates a form in a builder that works like a document, adds fields (text, required marks, logic, a grid, a rating), and keeps it in Draft with Publish ready.
steal: A Draft label with Preview and Publish stays in the header until publishing, so it is clear the checklist is not live yet (screens 1-8).
A When/Then rule under a field hides or disables later questions without a separate rules page (screen 5).
The blank page offers 'Start from scratch' or 'Use a template' (screens 2-3).
Asterisks on block titles mark required items, which rubric items need (screens 5-8).
avoid: Payment, wallet and Stripe blocks in the middle of a checklist are noise for sim evaluation forms (screens 7-8).
tally 908fac0b.fit: Scenario manager: extend Essentials checklist editing beyond the cut-down Case Manager, with one long page plus draft and publish instead of only tabbed SCE fields. It does not replace the Equipment tabs.

tally c7ec1d19.summary: After deleting an account, the person writes a reason in one open text box without logging in, submits, and sees a thank-you from the makers.
steal: Neither the form nor the thank-you page shows any account controls, so people can answer anonymously without logging in (screens 1-3).
A thank-you page with no further button is a clean end after a checklist is submitted (screen 3).
avoid: Tying the feedback to a finished account deletion is the wrong trigger for room or session feedback (screen 1).
tally c7ec1d19.fit: Scenario manager: borrow only the anonymous, no-login form and the thank-you page for the room-TV checklist opened by QR. It does not show a QR code and is not a session evaluation.

steal: One Share area puts 'Copy link' next to email, QR code and phone-preview options, so the TV QR code and the link are shared from one place (screen 2).
A 'Get the QR code' pop-up shows a large code and 'Download QR Code', for printing or showing on a room screen (screen 3).
A side menu offers 'Share the link', 'Embed in an email' and 'Embed in a web page', so the form reaches people in other ways without being rebuilt (screen 2).
Each question has a Required switch while the author edits, before publishing (screen 1).
avoid: Social sharing buttons and Canva thumbnails are marketing extras; sim-room checklists need practical ways out (TV, QR code, link) (screen 2).
typeform f8d34d78.fit: Scenario manager: the author side of a checklist opened by QR: create a link and a QR code to show in the room. A public link works for named or anonymous answers without login.

steal: The empty list offers to create a new template or import one, with 'Create' in two places.
A Draft label stays beside the title until the template is published.
The 'Publish New Version' pop-up shows '✓ No warnings' and asks you to slide to publish.
A blank page offers 'Pick a template', 'Upload HTML' and typed / commands to add content.
avoid: The extra slide-to-publish step should be kept for going live, not for every routine save of a scenario.
resend 8914ef26.fit: Scenario manager: add clear draft and published versions, with a check before publishing. It supports replacing Word and paper with a basic editor, not a Maestro rebuild.

steal: Version history opens as a side panel over the editor, so you do not leave the page.
The confirmation explains that restoring creates a new version and keeps the current content in the history.
Each history entry shows how long ago it was saved and who saved it.
After restoring, the template stays in Draft, so it still has to be published to go live.
resend 62ac5b2e.fit: Scenario manager: fills a known gap, because the SCE editor cannot restore old versions clearly. Restoring without losing anything protects faculty work, unlike today's checklists, which lose data when the window closes.

steal: Each lesson row shows whether it has content ('Empty' or '1 Text & Images') next to Publish or Published (screen 1).
The 'Add content' panel groups content blocks and teaching tools, with Quiz next to the media blocks (screen 2).
Each block opens in its own editor with Cancel and Save, instead of being edited on the long lesson page (screens 3-4).
A saved block is labelled TEXT & IMAGES with Edit and a drag handle, and the outline on the side marks the current lesson (screen 5).
avoid: Marketing tools (Upsell, Referrals) in the same 'Add content' list as teaching blocks should stay out of scenario building (screen 2).
teachable 98032d4a.fit: Scenario manager: grow Briefing from a single video into orientation and pre-brief material built from blocks. The outline and draft-to-publish steps mirror the SCE structure without replacing the tabbed Details, Objectives, Patient and Equipment form.

steal: A banner explains that grades will not be recorded on this plan, so it is clear answers are collected without scores (screens 3-4).
Each answer has a checkbox to mark it correct, allowing one or several correct answers, plus 'Add answer' (screens 3-4).
A finished question collapses and shows a check on the correct answer, while the next question stays open for editing (screen 6).
Each question can have an image, with alt text and a Replace option (screen 8).
avoid: Questions can only be added one at a time with '+ New question' and cannot be reused across quizzes, which is weak for faculty checklists that need shared item banks across scenarios (screens 6-8).
teachable 8c62da99.fit: Scenario manager: this supports checklists and knowledge checks for learners and faculty more than pre-brief videos. Quiz grading should stay lighter than the Enterprise Case Manager. Reusing items across scenarios is missing and needed.

google-ai-studio 4f2fdd14.summary: In a multi-speaker playground, the user writes a dialogue with general style instructions, alternating lines for Speaker 1 and Speaker 2, and a name and voice for each speaker.
steal: General style instructions stay separate from each speaker's lines.
Each line has a colour-coded speaker label, and '+ Add dialog' adds the next line.
A settings panel on the right renames a role once and picks its voice, and every line updates.
A plain-text view next to the script builder can serve as a printable cue card.
avoid: The text-to-speech voice settings and the Run button that generates audio are not needed, because Essentials needs cue cards for people (SP, operator), not synthetic speech.
google-ai-studio 4f2fdd14.fit: Scenario manager: a deliberately basic script builder per role for SP and sim-operator lines, in line with the plan not to build a Maestro editor or a stage machine.

steal: The empty Lists page has 'Create' in two places (the header and a link on the page), so it is never hidden.
The add-items pop-up has 'Current list' and 'Buy it again' tabs, and an empty 'Buy it again' tab offers to browse categories.
Search shows popular items with pictures before you type, and you tick several before tapping Done.
The list header has lock and share options, and the description under the title works like setup notes.
avoid: Having to choose a cover photo before adding items is an extra step a tech's prep list does not need.
instacart 94df2baf.fit: Scenario manager: move today's free-text Equipment & Supplies toward picking from a catalog into a named list with notes. Stock and check-out stay in Inventory, as planned.

luma 024a7f32.summary: An event host opens the check-in scanner, points the camera at a guest's QR code, confirms the guest's details, and checks them in.
steal: Clear wording ('Point the camera at a ticket QR code') tells the host exactly what to scan (screens 1, 3).
A panel shows the guest's name, email and status before 'Check In' is tapped (screen 2).
A short 'Guest checked in' message appears while the scanner stays open, which keeps a queue moving (screen 3).
A switch between List and Scan, plus search, gives a way out when scanning fails (screens 1, 3).
avoid: Using a host who scans guest tickets as the model for room-TV feedback gets it backwards, because the wrong person holds the code.
luma 024a7f32.fit: Scenario manager: the opposite of the Essentials QR checklist, where a learner's phone reads a QR code on the TV without login. It is only loosely relevant to staff checking attendance at the door.
